title: Choose ShipBrief’s visual world
question: You asked for a bolder, dimensional direction with real 3D objects and motion. Choose one direction for all six views, or reroll again.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.lineage: Glass spectrogram instruments and calibrated spectral rails
options.thesis: One spectral rail maps a push from incoming code through evidence to a draft for human review.
options.viewport: A small 3D spectrogram sits above one off-center navigation rail; a doubled sodium line slides to Review while the selected push opens into a readable evidence-and-draft plate.
options.risk: The instrumentation can feel too esoteric; every state keeps a plain text label and the 3D object stays secondary.

raised.raise: The selected push lifts forward while surrounding activity dims, making focus unmistakable.
Completed stages remain visible along the rail; progress never erases earlier evidence.
The active route gets a continuous, gently bending path instead of another nested dashboard.

options.label: Acetate Reference Manual
options.lineage: Tabbed software manuals and punched acetate overlays
options.thesis: Commit evidence and its draft sit on clear, hinged layers over one vivid section board.
options.viewport: A 3D acetate leaf lifts over the selected push; clear source tabs expose linked commits while the draft and human review controls remain fully readable.
options.case: Beats the leader on both axes: technical manuals are familiar to app builders, and layered source leaves make the evidence-to-draft relationship explicit.
options.risk: Layering can create visual overlap; only the selected leaf stays clear and interactive.

options.label: Streaming Title-Card Wall
options.lineage: Streaming catalog rows and expanding title cards
options.thesis: Each push is a focused title card that lifts forward to reveal its evidence and draft.
options.viewport: Horizontal rows of 3D push tiles keep context visible; focus lifts one push and reveals its commits, compare link, draft, and review actions.
options.case: Holds product clarity: the selected push expands into evidence and review, though catalog browsing is less familiar to builders than the spectral rail.
options.risk: The visual catalog could overemphasize decorative objects; each tile remains primarily a commit summary.

options.label: Design Annual Plate
options.lineage: Design annuals and publication plate sections
options.thesis: A dimensional publication plate presents a draft with registration marks for its source evidence.
options.viewport: One large 3D proof plate carries the draft; linked commits occupy its margin and the review decision anchors the sheet below.
options.case: Holds product clarity: the plate maps evidence to edited copy well, but publication design speaks less directly to app builders than the leader.
options.risk: A single plate can feel like a read-only artifact unless edit and approval controls stay prominent.

options.label: Jet-Age Ticket Wallet
options.lineage: Airline ticket wallets, carbon copies, and baggage tags
options.case: Fuses weakly: travel booking is less familiar to app builders and coupons suggest a one-time transaction.
options.kept: Progress stays legible as a sequence, and completed stages remain visible instead of disappearing.

options.label: Zoo and Gardens Guide Map
options.lineage: Fold-out zoo and garden guide maps
options.case: Fuses weakly: a park-map world does not help builders recognize code evidence or draft review.
options.kept: A continuous route can show the end-to-end push-to-review journey.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar app workspace puts pending draft review first, with evidence and settings one click away.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional overview shows the draft queue, selected commit evidence, and a small animated 3D push-to-draft model.
canonCard.risk: Intentionally familiar; the interface itself carries little distinctive identity.
